html:
The heavyweight boxing title fight of 30 October 1974 in Kinshasa, capital of Zaire, in which Muhammad Ali knocked out the champion George Foreman in the eighth round.

The promoter Don King arranged it, and Mobutu paid much of the cost to put Zaire on the world map. The fight was held before dawn so it could be seen live in America. Foreman was younger, stronger and the favourite. Ali leaned back on the ropes and let Foreman punch himself out, a tactic he called "rope-a-dope", then knocked him down. The crowd chanted "Ali, bomaye", "Ali, kill him".

Ali, who had been stripped of his title in 1967 for refusing to be drafted during the Vietnam War, became champion again. For many Africans the fight was a moment of Black pride on African soil. A music festival, Zaire 74, brought James Brown, B. B. King and Miriam Makeba to Kinshasa. The documentary When We Were Kings (1996) told the story. Hundreds of millions are thought to have watched the fight worldwide.
sum: The heavyweight boxing title fight of 30 October 1974 in Kinshasa, capital of Zaire, in which Muhammad Ali knocked out the champion George Foreman in the eighth round.
